seo.title: Trino client for {devices}
seo.description: Query across Trino catalogs, sign in with a password, a JWT or a client certificate over TLS, read logical and distributed plans, and cancel a query.

header.title: Trino client for {devices}
header.lead: Join tables from different catalogs in one query, read the plan Trino will run, and stop a runaway query on the coordinator. What a write can do depends on the connector behind each catalog.

sections.title: Connect and sign in
paragraphs: Enter the coordinator’s host and port and a <ui>Username</ui>, the user your queries run as. <ui>Catalog</ui> and <ui>Schema</ui> are optional starting points; leave Catalog empty to browse every catalog. An IANA <ui>Time Zone</ui> in the Options section sets the session’s zone.

Sign in with a password, sent as HTTP Basic for LDAP or password-file authentication, or with a JWT access token sent as a bearer credential. Either one goes only over TLS: with SSL Disabled, a connection that holds one is refused before anything is sent. A client certificate and key on the SSL pane add mutual TLS.

SSL starts Disabled, which is plain HTTP; every other mode forces TLS with no plaintext fallback, and port 443 turns on Verify Identity. A redirect from a proxy in front of the coordinator is never followed; the error names where it pointed. Reach a coordinator behind a bastion through an SSH tunnel, and bring a trino:// URL in with Import from URL….

sections.title: Query across catalogs
paragraphs: A connection opens on a catalog and schema, and any query can still name catalog.schema.table in full, such as a join between a Hive table and a PostgreSQL table. The sidebar expands each catalog into schemas and tables, with materialized views beside tables and views and row counts from SHOW STATS.
bigint and decimal are read as exact text, not floating point. varbinary shows as hex, array, map and row as JSON, and timestamps keep the value the server returned.

<explain>Explain</explain> offers Logical, Distributed, IO, Validate and Analyze. Validate checks a query without running it, Analyze runs it and reports actual timings, and every plan comes back as raw text.

SET SESSION holds for the rest of the connection. Query > Cancel Query tells the coordinator to kill the running query, and that is the way to stop one: the connection’s query timeout does not reach Trino.

<editing>Cell edits</editing> become INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE, each value carrying its Trino type. Trino reports no primary keys, so an edit matches on every column of the row as it was read, with no transaction to roll it back. Editing one of two identical rows changes both; check for duplicates first.

sections.title: Structure
paragraphs: The <structure>Structure tab</structure> creates tables and adds, drops, renames and retypes columns, in autocommit. Whether a change runs is up to the catalog’s connector, and a type change is the one fewest connectors accept.

sections.title: Move data
paragraphs: There is no import. <export>Export</export> a table or a result as {exportFormats}.

faq.question: Why does a valid statement come back as NOT_SUPPORTED?
faq.answer: The connector behind that catalog does not implement the operation, whatever Trino’s grammar allows. A read-only connector refuses every write. Check the connector’s own documentation for what it supports.

faq.question: Can I use an encrypted client key?
faq.answer: No. Trino connections have no key passphrase field. Write a decrypted copy with openssl pkey -in encrypted.key -out client.key and choose that file.
